title: Graph scalability: chains, grids and random networks
summary: Generated thermal graphs from 100 nodes up (to 100,000 under --full), on the serial, thread-pool and partitioned backends, under Euler node by node and Runge–Kutta 4: the same numbers bit for bit on every backend, the engine's work as counted, the method's exact steps to rounding, and the exact solution's error; under --full, wall time, throughput, peak memory, parallel speed-up and the time to load, compile and solve.

infeasible.reason: A project of a million nodes is about 1.45 GB of JSON (about 1,450 bytes a node with its two relationships), more than one JavaScript string can hold, so the project encoder cannot write it; the engine's validation alone would take about six minutes (about 0.33 ms a node, measured at 10,000 and 100,000 nodes), and the 8 GB machine these benchmarks were written on could not hold the document while the engine parses it.
